sa86dd4c4376a47: CNCF Case Study: How Korea's NAVER-owned subsidiary SNOW Corp. used HAMi to achieve GPU sharing, KEDA to achieve active automatic scaling up and respond to 700% viral traffic peaks - 91% reduction in MTTR, 85% reduction in peak traffic errors, $17.4 million estimated cost savings.
s2b8b0fc880ecfb: The division of HAMi and KEDA
s00f517895d70e4: SNOW Corp. is a subsidiary of the Korean NAVER group, which operates a 1000+Screen A100 GPU calculation cluster that provides AI functionality to the top three global-ranked GenAI applications: SNOW, EPIK, B612, covering 200 million + users worldwide. Infrastructure loads 1,200+AI workflow and 400+ models.

s96b6dde334be23: SNOW moves up to the localised Kubernetes platform, using a decorated External ETC CD pop-up secure high availability. The entire technology repository is supported by CNCF Ecology: CNI, Helm achieves Gitops deployment, Traefik as Ingress, Prometheus/Loki/Grafana provides access,
sc370441b13a61c: Kubernetes Default Scheduler enforces strict GPU integration, which prevents SNOW sequenced training - migration of inference flow lines - trainers and inference engines must share the same GPU. Hami solves this problem through virtualization GPU resources (vGPU), enabling multiple containers in the same Pod to share a single GPU. It is integrated with kube-schedulers without any need for modification of application codes and fully compatible with the wider automatic stretching ecology.
s62020ccf423d3e: Standard indicators (CPU/RAM, DCGM utilization) are unreliable for the heterogeneous load of SNOW, and the built-in RabbitMQ Zoomer within KEDA serves as a lag indicator - taking into account about 60 seconds of model preheating time, it is always too late to trigger scaling after queue backlogs have been formed.

s24513cf8a17bde: Respond to 700% traffic peaks by mixing cloud elasticity
s9d2efe8cbe149a: On Saturday morning, the gypsy filter suddenly burst into fire three hours ago, and traffic soared to three times as fast as local compute resourcees. SNOW immediately expanded its load elasticity to cloud service providers through a unified Gitops stream line, using the same Helm Charts for all clusters, with cloud nodes pulling directly from central RabitMQ teams — the entire process was broken. It successfully digested seven times the peak flow, taking full advantage of this business opportunity.

s5db00ac06d6cf9: The cloud-native transition of SNOW Corp. demonstrates how to combine Kubernetes with the wider CNCF ecology, overcoming the fundamental limitations of GPU production and observability at extreme scales. By introducing Hami GPU sharing, and using active self-defined indicators to enhance KEDA, SNOW, from passive manual operations to predictive automation. This architecture not only allows the platform to absorb 700% of the peak volume of traffic that has been uninterruptedly mixed environmental expansion, but also achieves significant improvements in cost efficiency, reliability and operating speed.
